Assembly-Unload-Diagnostics.html.title: Assembly Unload Diagnostics Guide | CatSweeper Documentation
Assembly-Unload-Diagnostics.html.summary: Assembly Unload Diagnostics Guide Based on Microsoft Documentation: How to use and debug assembly unloadability in .NET Problem Godot C# hot-reload fails with: ERROR: modules/mono/mono_gd/gd_mono.cpp:791 - .NET: Failed to unload assemblies. This happens when references prevent the CLR from unloading the assembly. Installation The plugin is located at addons/AssemblyUnloadDiagnostics/. Open Project → Project Settings → Plugins Find "Assembly Unload Diagnostics" and enable it Two buttons will appear in the editor toolbar: 🔍 Quick - Fast check for common blockers 🔬 Full - Complete diagnostic scan Diagnostic Tools 1. Diagnostics (Static Class) Static utility class that analyzes your code for common unload blockers. Quick Check (Automatic) Runs automatically when the plugin unloads (e.g., before rebuild): using AssemblyUnloadDiagnostics; // Manual quick check Diagnostics.QuickCheck(); Manual Full Diagnostics using AssemblyUnloadDiagnostics; // Run complete diagnostics Diagnostics.RunFullDiagnostics(); // Or individual checks: Diagnostics.ListLoadedAssemblies(); Diagnostics.TestUnloadability(); Diagnostics.QuickCheck(); Configure Assembly Patterns // Add your own assembly patterns to check Diagnostics.AssemblyPatterns.Add("MyCustomAssembly"); 2. ReferenceTracker Track specific objects to verify they get garbage collected. using AssemblyUnloadDiagnostics; // Track objects you suspect might cause issues public class MyClass : IDisposable { public MyClass() { ReferenceTracker.Track("MyClass.instance", this); // Or use extension method: _myObject = new SomeObject().TrackForUnload("MyObject"); } public void Dispose() { ReferenceTracker.Untrack("MyClass.instance"); } } // Check which objects are still alive after GC ReferenceTracker.CheckAliveReferences(); 3. Toolbar Buttons 🔍 Quick - Runs QuickCheck() and ReferenceTracker.CheckAliveReferences() 🔬 Full - Runs all diagnostics including assembly listing and unloadability test Common Blockers 1. Static Fields with Object References // ❌ BAD - holds reference preventing unload private static MyService _instance; // ✅ GOOD - clear on cleanup public static void Clear() => _instance = null; 2. Event Subscriptions Not Unsubscribed // ❌ BAD SomeEvent += MyHandler; // ✅ GOOD public void Dispose() { SomeEvent -= MyHandler; } 3. Lambda Captures // ❌ BAD - captures 'this' implicitly someCollection.Where(x => x.Value == this.MyValue); // ✅ GOOD - static lambda, no capture someCollection.Where(static x => x.Value > 0); 4. Async Operations Not Completed // ❌ BAD - async task may still hold references async void StartSomething() { await SomeAsyncWork(); // If not completed, holds references } // ✅ GOOD - ensure async work completes or is cancelled await _cancellationTokenSource.CancelAsync(); 5. Timers and Threads // ❌ BAD - timer holds callback reference _timer = new Timer(_ => DoWork(), null, 0, 1000); // ✅ GOOD - dispose timer public void Dispose() { _timer?.Dispose(); } Debugging Workflow Enable diagnostics: AssemblyCleanup.DiagnosticsEnabled = true; Track suspicious objects: ReferenceTracker.Track("StageSession", stageSession); Build and watch console output: Look for ⚠ ALIVE: messages - these are potential blockers Look for [STATIC] and [DELEGATE] warnings Fix identified issues: Clear static references Unsubscribe from events Dispose resources Use static lambdas where possible Verify fix: Rebuild and check if unload succeeds Check ✓ COLLECTED: messages Example Output ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ ASSEMBLY UNLOAD DIAGNOSTICS ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ [1] Checking Static Fields... [OBJECT] GameDebugger._instance: GameDebugger ⚠ [DELEGATE] StageSession._OnGridUpdated holds delegate: Dispatch └─ Target: StageController (prevents unload!) [2] Checking Event Subscriptions... ⚠ [EVENT] SomeService.OnUpdate has 2 subscribers └─ Subscriber: StageController.HandleUpdate ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Total potential blockers found: 2 ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Workarounds If you can't find the blocker, you can: Disable hot-reload in .csproj: <PropertyGroup> <GodotDisableHotReload>true</GodotDisableHotReload> </PropertyGroup> Disable in Editor Settings: Editor → Editor Settings → Dotnet → Editor → Reload Assemblies On Build → false Restart editor after each rebuild (safest option) Further Reading Microsoft: Assembly Unloadability Godot Issue #78513 .NET AssemblyLoadContext

GameDebuggerUtil-Usage.html.title: GameDebuggerUtil - JSON ↔ Variant Conversion | CatSweeper Documentation
GameDebuggerUtil-Usage.html.summary: GameDebuggerUtil - JSON ↔ Variant Conversion Overview GameDebuggerUtil provides bidirectional conversion between JSON objects and Godot Variants, enabling seamless data exchange between C# and Godot types. Features ✅ Convert Godot → JSON Converts Godot Variants to JSON-serializable objects Handles Vector2, Vector2I, Dictionary, Array Preserves type information where possible ✅ Parse JSON → Godot Reconstructs Godot Variants from JSON objects Auto-detects Vector2/Vector2I from {x, y} objects Supports System.Text.Json.JsonElement Handles nested structures API Reference Godot → JSON Conversion // Convert a single Variant to JSON object object ConvertVariantToJson(Variant variant) // Convert Godot Array to object[] object[] ConvertArrayToJson(Godot.Collections.Array array) // Convert Godot Dictionary to C# Dictionary Dictionary<string, object> ConvertDictionaryToJson(Godot.Collections.Dictionary dict) JSON → Godot Conversion // Parse JSON object to Variant Variant ParseJsonToVariant(object jsonObj) // Parse JSON array to Godot Array Godot.Collections.Array ParseJsonToArray(object[] jsonArray) // Parse JSON dictionary to Godot Dictionary Godot.Collections.Dictionary ParseJsonToDictionary(Dictionary<string, object> jsonDict) Usage Examples Example 1: Convert Godot Data to JSON // Godot data var position = new Vector2I(10, 20); var data = new Godot.Collections.Array { position, "player", 100 }; // Convert to JSON var jsonArray = GameDebuggerUtil.ConvertArrayToJson(data); var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(jsonArray); // Result: [[{"x":10,"y":20},"player","100"]] Example 2: Parse JSON back to Godot // JSON data var json = """{"x": 10, "y": 20}"""; var jsonObj = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Dictionary<string, object>>(json); // Convert to Godot Variant var variant = GameDebuggerUtil.ParseJsonToVariant(jsonObj); var position = variant.AsVector2I(); // Vector2I(10, 20) Example 3: Complex Nested Data // Godot data with nested structures var gameState = new Godot.Collections.Dictionary { ["player"] = new Godot.Collections.Dictionary { ["position"] = new Vector2(100.5f, 200.3f), ["health"] = 100, ["inventory"] = new Godot.Collections.Array { "sword", "shield" } }, ["level"] = 5 }; // Convert to JSON var jsonDict = GameDebuggerUtil.ConvertDictionaryToJson(gameState); var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(jsonDict); // Parse back to Godot var parsedDict = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Dictionary<string, object>>(json); var godotDict = GameDebuggerUtil.ParseJsonToDictionary(parsedDict); Example 4: Working with JsonElement // Receive JSON from WebSocket var jsonText = """{"position": {"x": 50, "y": 100}, "name": "Player"}"""; var document = JsonDocument.Parse(jsonText); // Convert JsonElement to Variant var variant = GameDebuggerUtil.ParseJsonToVariant(document.RootElement); var dict = variant.AsGodotDictionary(); // Access nested data var positionVariant = dict["position"]; var position = positionVariant.AsVector2I(); // Vector2I(50, 100) Type Conversion Table Godot Type JSON Representation Notes Vector2I(10, 20) {"x": 10, "y": 20} Integer coordinates Vector2(10.5, 20.3) {"x": 10.5, "y": 20.3} Float coordinates Dictionary { "key": value } Recursive conversion Array [item1, item2] Recursive conversion string "text" Direct conversion int, long, float, double 123, 45.67 Direct conversion bool true, false Direct conversion null null Default Variant Auto-Detection Logic Vector2 vs Vector2I Detection When parsing {"x": ..., "y": ...} objects: Vector2I - If both x and y are integers {"x": 10, "y": 20} → Vector2I(10, 20) Vector2 - If either x or y has decimals {"x": 10.5, "y": 20} → Vector2(10.5, 20) Dictionary vs Vector Detection If object has exactly 2 properties named "x" and "y" → Vector Otherwise → Dictionary Integration with GameDebugger The utility is used internally by GameDebugger for WebSocket communication: // In GameDebugger.SendMessage var payload = new DebugMessage { Message = "stage_info", Data = GameDebuggerUtil.ConvertArrayToJson(data) }; var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(payload); await _client.SendText(json); // In GameToolsPlugin.OnMessageReceived var json = Encoding.UTF8.GetString(socketMessage.data.Span); var message = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<DebugMessage>(json); // message.Data is now ready to be parsed back to Godot Variant var godotData = GameDebuggerUtil.ParseJsonToVariant(message.Data); Performance Considerations Memory Allocation ConvertToJson: Creates new object arrays/dictionaries ParseToVariant: Creates new Godot collections For high-frequency messages, consider object pooling Type Detection Overhead Vector detection requires checking object properties Minimal overhead for most use cases Consider explicit type hints for performance-critical code Error Handling The utility is designed to be fault-tolerant: Null values: Return default Variant Unknown types: Convert to string via ToString() Invalid structures: Gracefully degrade to simpler types Best Practices Use for WebSocket/Network communication where JSON is required Avoid for internal Godot-to-Godot communication (use Variants directly) Validate data types after parsing if type safety is critical Cache frequently used conversions if performance is a concern Future Enhancements Potential additions: Support for more Godot types (Vector3, Color, Rect2, etc.) Custom serialization attributes Schema validation Performance optimizations with object pooling

GameDesign/Cat Sweeper/踩地雷玩法/Fever Mode.title: Fever Mode | CatSweeper Documentation
GameDesign/Cat Sweeper/踩地雷玩法/Fever Mode.summary: Fever Mode 每開一個格可以獲得能量（Fever Energy） 每格獲得的能量為固定比例，於game setting設定EnergyMultiplier，暫定5% 如因相連空格而大範圍打開空格會一次計算所有格子*5% 成功打開地雷會增加固定比例，於Game Setting設定CatchSucessEnergyMultiplier，暫定10% 能量會逐漸減少，速度於game setting設定EnergyDecreaseSpeed，暫定1%/秒 每能量滿100%會進入Fever Mode 於Fever Mode中玩家可以任意點擊格子，即使打開Mine Level > Player Level的Mine也不會扣HP Fever Mode期間打開格子的增加量同樣於gamesetting 設定FeverModeEnergyMultiplier，暫定0% Fever Mode期間打開能量會逐漸減少，速度於game setting設定FeverModeEnergyDecreaseSpeed，暫定為20%/秒 能量歸0會離開Fever Mode 離開Fever Mode時需要UI 支援，並map 會暫停0.2秒 input避免玩家錯誤撳到地雷

WebSocket-Debugger-Migration.html.title: WebSocket-Based Debugger Migration | CatSweeper Documentation
WebSocket-Debugger-Migration.html.summary: WebSocket-Based Debugger Migration Overview Successfully replaced the EngineDebugger workflow with a WebSocket-based client/server architecture to avoid the known issue where EngineDebugger loses binding when the solution is rebuilt. Architecture Editor Side (GameToolsPlugin) WebSocket Server: Starts when the plugin enters the tree on port 8080 Message Router: Routes incoming messages to appropriate GameToolWindow instances based on channel names Protocol: JSON-based messages with format { "Message": "channel:message_name", "Data": [...] } Runtime Side (GameDebugger) WebSocket Client: Singleton instance that connects to editor on port 8080 Async Connection: Connects asynchronously when the game starts Message Sending: Converts Godot types to JSON and sends via WebSocket Files Modified 1. CatSweeper.csproj Added reference to Modules\WsConnect\WsConnect\WsConnect.csproj 2. GameToolsPlugin.cs (addons/GameTools/) Changes: Removed GameToolsDebuggerPlugin dependency Added WsServer instance Added GameToolsMessageRouter for routing messages Implemented WebSocket server lifecycle (start/stop) Added message handlers: OnClientConnected, OnClientDisconnected, OnMessageReceived 3. GameToolsMessageRouter.cs (NEW - addons/GameTools/) Purpose: Routes WebSocket messages to appropriate GameToolWindow instances Converts JSON data back to Godot types (Array, Dictionary, Vector2I, etc.) Handles complex type conversions from JsonElement to Variant Key Methods: RegisterWindow(): Registers a GameToolWindow for a specific channel RouteMessage(): Parses message format "channel:message_name" and routes to window ConvertToGodotArray(): Converts JSON arrays to Godot Arrays ConvertJsonElementToGodotValue(): Handles all JSON type conversions 4. GameDebugger.cs (NEW - Script/Core/) Purpose: Singleton runtime debugger that replaces EngineDebugger Connects to editor WebSocket server at ws://localhost:8080 Sends debug messages from game to editor Key Methods: Instance: Singleton accessor IsActive(): Returns true if connected to editor ConnectAsync(): Establishes WebSocket connection SendMessage(): Sends messages in format "channel:message_name" with Godot Array data ConvertArrayToJson(): Converts Godot types to JSON-serializable objects ConvertVariantToJson(): Handles Variant type conversions (Vector2I, Dictionary, Array, etc.) 5. StageController.cs (Script/Stage/) Changes: Added using CatSweeper.Core; for GameDebugger In _Ready(): Calls GameDebugger.Instance.ConnectAsync() under #if TOOLS Replaced EngineDebugger.SendMessage() with GameDebugger.Instance.SendMessage() in two locations: stage:stage_initialized message stage:grid_updated message Message Flow From Game to Editor: Game calls GameDebugger.Instance.SendMessage("stage:grid_updated", data) GameDebugger converts Godot types to JSON Message sent via WsClient to WebSocket server GameToolsPlugin receives message GameToolsMessageRouter parses channel name Message routed to appropriate GameToolWindow (e.g., StageSessionWindow) Window's OnMessageCaptured() method processes the data Message Format: { "Message": "channel:message_name", "Data": [/* array of converted Godot types */] } Type Conversions Godot → JSON (GameDebugger): Vector2I/Vector2 → { x: number, y: number } Dictionary → { [key: string]: any } Array → any[] Primitives → string/number/boolean JSON → Godot (GameToolsMessageRouter): { x: number, y: number } → Vector2I JSON Object → Godot.Collections.Dictionary JSON Array → Godot.Collections.Array Primitives → int/long/double/string/bool Benefits No Rebuild Issues: WebSocket connection persists across solution rebuilds Decoupled: Editor and runtime communicate via standard WebSocket protocol Flexible: Can add new channels/windows without modifying core infrastructure Debuggable: Can inspect WebSocket traffic with standard tools Extensible: Easy to add new message types and handlers Usage In Runtime Code: #if TOOLS GameDebugger.Instance.SendMessage("channel:message_name", new Array() { data1, data2, new Dictionary { { "key", value } } }); #endif In Editor Plugin: public class MyToolWindow : GameToolWindow { public override string channelName => "mychannel"; public override string tabName => "My Tool"; public override bool OnMessageCaptured(string message, Array data, int sessionId) { if (message == "message_name") { // Handle the message return true; } return false; } } Testing Build succeeded with 0 errors and 140 warnings (all pre-existing). WsConnect-Dynamic-Buffer.html.title: Dynamic Buffer Size in WsServer and WsClient | CatSweeper Documentation
WsConnect-Dynamic-Buffer.html.summary: Dynamic Buffer Size in WsServer and WsClient Overview Both WsServer and WsClient now use dynamic buffering to handle WebSocket messages of any size efficiently. How It Works Previous Implementation (Fixed Buffer) // Old approach - limited to bufferSize bytes var buffer = new byte[bufferSize]; var result = await ws.ReceiveAsync(buffer, token); // If message > bufferSize, it would be truncated! New Implementation (Dynamic Buffer) // New approach - handles messages of any size var chunkBuffer = new byte[bufferSize]; // Fixed chunk size for reading var messageBuffer = new List<byte>(); // Dynamic accumulator do { result = await ws.ReceiveAsync(new ArraySegment<byte>(chunkBuffer), token); // Append chunk to message buffer for (int i = 0; i < result.Count; i++) { messageBuffer.Add(chunkBuffer[i]); } } while (!result.EndOfMessage); // Keep reading until complete message var completeMessage = messageBuffer.ToArray(); Key Improvements 1. Handles Large Messages Messages larger than the initial bufferSize are now fully received No data loss or truncation Memory grows dynamically as needed 2. Efficient for Small Messages Small messages don't waste memory Only allocates what's needed for the actual message size 3. Chunk-Based Reading Reads data in fixed-size chunks (configurable via constructor) Default chunk size: 1024 bytes Can be adjusted based on your typical message size 4. EndOfMessage Detection Uses WebSocket's built-in EndOfMessage flag Ensures complete messages are received before processing Prevents partial message handling Configuration The bufferSize parameter now represents the chunk size for reading: // Small messages (e.g., JSON commands) var server = new WsServer("http://localhost:8080/", bufferSize: 1024); // Large messages (e.g., file transfers) var server = new WsServer("http://localhost:8080/", bufferSize: 8192); // Custom chunk size var server = new WsServer("http://localhost:8080/", bufferSize: 4096); Choosing the Right Chunk Size Use Case Recommended Chunk Size Reason JSON messages (< 10KB) 1024 - 2048 bytes Minimizes memory overhead Binary data (10KB - 100KB) 4096 - 8192 bytes Balances throughput and memory File transfers (> 100KB) 8192 - 16384 bytes Maximizes throughput Memory Characteristics Memory Usage Pattern Message Size: 5KB, Chunk Size: 1024 bytes Iteration 1: chunkBuffer[1024] + messageBuffer[1024] = ~2KB Iteration 2: chunkBuffer[1024] + messageBuffer[2048] = ~3KB Iteration 3: chunkBuffer[1024] + messageBuffer[3072] = ~4KB Iteration 4: chunkBuffer[1024] + messageBuffer[4096] = ~5KB Iteration 5: chunkBuffer[1024] + messageBuffer[5120] = ~6KB (final) Peak Memory: ~6KB (vs fixed 5KB for exact-size buffer) Memory Trade-offs Advantages: ✅ No message size limits ✅ Adapts to actual message sizes ✅ Small overhead per message Disadvantages: ⚠️ Slight memory overhead from List<byte> growth ⚠️ Some GC pressure from intermediate allocations Performance Optimization Tips 1. Reuse Message Buffer (Advanced) If you're processing many messages, consider using ArrayPool: private async Task ReceiveMessagesAsync(WebSocket ws, CancellationToken token) { var chunkBuffer = ArrayPool<byte>.Shared.Rent(bufferSize); var messageBuffer = new List<byte>(bufferSize); try { while (ws.State == WebSocketState.Open) { messageBuffer.Clear(); WebSocketReceiveResult result; do { result = await ws.ReceiveAsync( new ArraySegment<byte>(chunkBuffer, 0, bufferSize), token); messageBuffer.AddRange( new ArraySegment<byte>(chunkBuffer, 0, result.Count)); } while (!result.EndOfMessage); // Process messageBuffer... } } finally { ArrayPool<byte>.Shared.Return(chunkBuffer); } } 2. Pre-allocate Message Buffer If you know the typical message size: var messageBuffer = new List<byte>(expectedMessageSize); 3. Adjust Chunk Size Based on Network Local network (low latency): Smaller chunks (1-2KB) Internet (higher latency): Larger chunks (4-8KB) Example Usage Sending Large Messages // Server can now receive messages of any size var largeData = new byte[1024 * 1024]; // 1MB await client.SendAsync(largeData, SocketMessage.Type.Binary); // Server will receive it in chunks and reassemble Receiving Messages // Client receives complete message regardless of size var message = await client.Receive(); Console.WriteLine($"Received {message.data.Length} bytes"); Testing Test Case: Large Message [Test] public async Task TestLargeMessage() { var server = new WsServer("http://localhost:8080/", bufferSize: 1024); server.Start(); var client = new WsClient("ws://localhost:8080", bufferSize: 1024); await client.Connect(); // Send 100KB message with 1KB chunks var largeMessage = new byte[100 * 1024]; new Random().NextBytes(largeMessage); await client.Send(largeMessage); // Should receive complete message var received = await server.Receive(); Assert.Equal(100 * 1024, received.data.Length); } Migration Guide No code changes required! The API remains the same: // Old code still works var server = new WsServer("http://localhost:8080/"); server.OnMessageReceived += (client, msg) => { Console.WriteLine($"Received: {msg.data.Length} bytes"); }; // Messages of any size are now handled automatically Compatibility ✅ Backward compatible with existing code ✅ Works with all WebSocket message types (Text, Binary) ✅ Handles fragmented messages transparently ✅ No breaking changes to public API Summary The dynamic buffer implementation provides: Unlimited message size support Memory efficiency for small messages Configurable chunk size for performance tuning Zero breaking changes to existing code Your WebSocket connections can now handle messages of any size without modification!

Name Description IInputTouchListener listener | Edit this page View Source _Input(InputEvent) Called when there is an input event. The input event propagates up through the node tree until a node consumes it. It is only called if input processing is enabled, which is done automatically if this method is overridden, and can be toggled with SetProcessInput(bool). To consume the input event and stop it propagating further to other nodes, Godot.Viewport.SetInputAsHandled() can be called. For gameplay input, Godot.Node._UnhandledInput(Godot.InputEvent) and Godot.Node._UnhandledKeyInput(Godot.InputEvent) are usually a better fit as they allow the GUI to intercept the events first. Note: This method is only called if the node is present in the scene tree (i.e. if it's not an orphan). node and its children have entered the scene tree. If the node has children, their Godot.Node._Ready() callbacks get triggered first, and the parent node will receive the ready notification afterwards. Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationReady notification in _Notification(int). See also the @onready annotation for variables. Usually used for initialization. For even earlier initialization, Godot.GodotObject.GodotObject() may be used. See also Godot.Node._EnterTree(). Note: This method may be called only once for each node. After removing a node from the scene tree and adding it again, Godot.Node._Ready() will not be called a second time. This can be bypassed by requesting another call with Godot.Node.RequestReady(), which may be called anywhere before adding the node again. Parameters Type Name Description ILogger logger | Edit this page View Source _Process(double) Called on each idle frame, prior to rendering, and after physics ticks have been processed. delta is the time between frames in seconds. It is only called if processing is enabled for this Node, which is done automatically if this method is overridden, and can be toggled with SetProcess(bool). Processing happens in order of Godot.Node.ProcessPriority, lower priority values are called first. Nodes with the same priority are processed in tree order, or top to bottom as seen in the editor (also known as pre-order traversal). Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationProcess notification in _Notification(int). Note: This method is only called if the node is present in the scene tree (i.e. if it's not an orphan). Note: When the engine is struggling and the frame rate is lowered, delta will increase. When delta is increased, it's capped at a maximum of Godot.Engine.TimeScale * Godot.Engine.MaxPhysicsStepsPerFrame / Godot.Engine.PhysicsTicksPerSecond. As a result, accumulated delta may not represent real world time. Note: When --fixed-fps is enabled or the engine is running in Movie Maker mode (see Godot.MovieWriter), process delta will always be the same for every frame, regardless of how much time the frame took to render. Note: Frame delta may be post-processed by Godot.OS.DeltaSmoothing if this is enabled for the project. Called when the node is "ready", i.e. when both the node and its children have entered the scene tree. If the node has children, their Godot.Node._Ready() callbacks get triggered first, and the parent node will receive the ready notification afterwards. Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationReady notification in _Notification(int). See also the @onready annotation for variables. Usually used for initialization. For even earlier initialization, Godot.GodotObject.GodotObject() may be used. See also Godot.Node._EnterTree(). Note: This method may be called only once for each node. After removing a node from the scene tree and adding it again, Godot.Node._Ready() will not be called a second time. This can be bypassed by requesting another call with Godot.Node.RequestReady(), which may be called anywhere before adding the node again. override void _ClearNode() Overrides CustomPropertyDrawer._ClearNode() | Edit this page View Source _Ready() Called when the node is "ready", i.e. when both the node and its children have entered the scene tree. If the node has children, their Godot.Node._Ready() callbacks get triggered first, and the parent node will receive the ready notification afterwards. Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationReady notification in _Notification(int). See also the @onready annotation for variables. Usually used for initialization. For even earlier initialization, Godot.GodotObject.GodotObject() may be used. See also Godot.Node._EnterTree(). Note: This method may be called only once for each node. After removing a node from the scene tree and adding it again, Godot.Node._Ready() will not be called a second time. This can be bypassed by requesting another call with Godot.Node.RequestReady(), which may be called anywhere before adding the node again. progress Returns Type Description Task<Node> | Edit this page View Source _Process(double) Called on each idle frame, prior to rendering, and after physics ticks have been processed. delta is the time between frames in seconds. It is only called if processing is enabled for this Node, which is done automatically if this method is overridden, and can be toggled with SetProcess(bool). Processing happens in order of Godot.Node.ProcessPriority, lower priority values are called first. Nodes with the same priority are processed in tree order, or top to bottom as seen in the editor (also known as pre-order traversal). Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationProcess notification in _Notification(int). Note: This method is only called if the node is present in the scene tree (i.e. if it's not an orphan). Note: When the engine is struggling and the frame rate is lowered, delta will increase. When delta is increased, it's capped at a maximum of Godot.Engine.TimeScale * Godot.Engine.MaxPhysicsStepsPerFrame / Godot.Engine.PhysicsTicksPerSecond. As a result, accumulated delta may not represent real world time. Note: When --fixed-fps is enabled or the engine is running in Movie Maker mode (see Godot.MovieWriter), process delta will always be the same for every frame, regardless of how much time the frame took to render. Note: Frame delta may be post-processed by Godot.OS.DeltaSmoothing if this is enabled for the project. _Ready() Called when the node is "ready", i.e. when both the node and its children have entered the scene tree. If the node has children, their Godot.Node._Ready() callbacks get triggered first, and the parent node will receive the ready notification afterwards. Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationReady notification in _Notification(int). See also the @onready annotation for variables. Usually used for initialization. For even earlier initialization, Godot.GodotObject.GodotObject() may be used. See also Godot.Node._EnterTree(). Note: This method may be called only once for each node. After removing a node from the scene tree and adding it again, Godot.Node._Ready() will not be called a second time. This can be bypassed by requesting another call with Godot.Node.RequestReady(), which may be called anywhere before adding the node again. [ScriptPath("res://cfGodotEngine/tool/Condition/Conditional2D.cs")] public class Conditional2D : Node2D, IDisposable Methods | Edit this page View Source _Ready() Called when the node is "ready", i.e. when both the node and its children have entered the scene tree. If the node has children, their Godot.Node._Ready() callbacks get triggered first, and the parent node will receive the ready notification afterwards. Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationReady notification in _Notification(int). See also the @onready annotation for variables. Usually used for initialization. For even earlier initialization, Godot.GodotObject.GodotObject() may be used. See also Godot.Node._EnterTree(). Note: This method may be called only once for each node. After removing a node from the scene tree and adding it again, Godot.Node._Ready() will not be called a second time. This can be bypassed by requesting another call with Godot.Node.RequestReady(), which may be called anywhere before adding the node again. _EnterTree() Called when the node enters the Godot.SceneTree (e.g. upon instantiating, scene changing, or after calling AddChild(Node, bool, InternalMode) in a script). If the node has children, its Godot.Node._EnterTree() callback will be called first, and then that of the children. Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationEnterTree notification in _Notification(int). Declaration public override void _EnterTree() Overrides Godot.Node._EnterTree() | Edit this page View Source _ExitTree() Called when the node is about to leave the Godot.SceneTree (e.g. upon freeing, scene changing, or after calling Godot.Node.RemoveChild(Godot.Node) in a script). If the node has children, its Godot.Node._ExitTree() callback will be called last, after all its children have left the tree. Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationExitTree notification in _Notification(int) and signal Godot.Node.TreeExiting. To get notified when the node has already left the active tree, connect to the Godot.Node.TreeExited. entered the scene tree. If the node has children, their Godot.Node._Ready() callbacks get triggered first, and the parent node will receive the ready notification afterwards. Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationReady notification in _Notification(int). See also the @onready annotation for variables. Usually used for initialization. For even earlier initialization, Godot.GodotObject.GodotObject() may be used. See also Godot.Node._EnterTree(). Note: This method may be called only once for each node. After removing a node from the scene tree and adding it again, Godot.Node._Ready() will not be called a second time. This can be bypassed by requesting another call with Godot.Node.RequestReady(), which may be called anywhere before adding the node again. Edit this page View Source _Ready() Called when the node is "ready", i.e. when both the node and its children have entered the scene tree. If the node has children, their Godot.Node._Ready() callbacks get triggered first, and the parent node will receive the ready notification afterwards. Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationReady notification in _Notification(int). See also the @onready annotation for variables. Usually used for initialization. For even earlier initialization, Godot.GodotObject.GodotObject() may be used. See also Godot.Node._EnterTree(). Note: This method may be called only once for each node. After removing a node from the scene tree and adding it again, Godot.Node._Ready() will not be called a second time. This can be bypassed by requesting another call with Godot.Node.RequestReady(), which may be called anywhere before adding the node again. _Process(double) Called on each idle frame, prior to rendering, and after physics ticks have been processed. delta is the time between frames in seconds. It is only called if processing is enabled for this Node, which is done automatically if this method is overridden, and can be toggled with SetProcess(bool). Processing happens in order of Godot.Node.ProcessPriority, lower priority values are called first. Nodes with the same priority are processed in tree order, or top to bottom as seen in the editor (also known as pre-order traversal). Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationProcess notification in _Notification(int). Note: This method is only called if the node is present in the scene tree (i.e. if it's not an orphan). Note: When the engine is struggling and the frame rate is lowered, delta will increase. When delta is increased, it's capped at a maximum of Godot.Engine.TimeScale * Godot.Engine.MaxPhysicsStepsPerFrame / Godot.Engine.PhysicsTicksPerSecond. As a result, accumulated delta may not represent real world time. Note: When --fixed-fps is enabled or the engine is running in Movie Maker mode (see Godot.MovieWriter), process delta will always be the same for every frame, regardless of how much time the frame took to render. Note: Frame delta may be post-processed by Godot.OS.DeltaSmoothing if this is enabled for the project. Declaration public override void _Process(double delta) Parameters Type Name Description double delta Overrides Node._Process(double) | Edit this page View Source _Ready() Called when the node is "ready", i.e. when both the node and its children have entered the scene tree. If the node has children, their Godot.Node._Ready() callbacks get triggered first, and the parent node will receive the ready notification afterwards. Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationReady notification in _Notification(int). See also the @onready annotation for variables. Usually used for initialization. For even earlier initialization, Godot.GodotObject.GodotObject() may be used. See also Godot.Node._EnterTree(). Note: This method may be called only once for each node. After removing a node from the scene tree and adding it again, Godot.Node._Ready() will not be called a second time. This can be bypassed by requesting another call with Godot.Node.RequestReady(), which may be called anywhere before adding the node again. docs/how-to-create-map.html.title: How To Create Stage Map | CatSweeper Documentation
docs/how-to-create-map.html.summary: How To Create Stage Map Practical Steps Creating Map Resource File Navigate to Engine File System, there is a StageMapInfo. Right click the folder and select "Create New/Resource", then select StageMapData Select Info/StageMapInfo/StageMapInfo.tres, In the inspector Create a new item in the array, assign the newly created StageMapData into the array item. Editing Map Project has include a simple StageMapCreator for custom map creation in editor Open the StageMapCreator scene at Scene/Editor/StageMapCreator.tscn, you will see Select the StageMapCreator node, Assign the StageMapData created in Create Map Resource File into Config Data/Stage Map Data Select TileMapLayer Node, Godot TileMap Editor will show up in the bottom of the editor, draw the tile in scene in the Godot way Select StageMapCreator Node, click "Save Stage Map" Button, you will check the array elements in Floor Grids to validate, assign the Map Id and you are good to go! After entering the play mode once, you can check _Export/Info/StageMapInfo/data.json to validate the StageMapResourceInfo is parsed correctly into json file. Will provide a demo video soon

Clone the Repository git clone https://github.com/Bus-Fighter/CatSweeper.git cd CatSweeper 2. Open in Godot Launch Godot 4.4.1 (Mono) Click Import, and select the project.godot file Godot will generate the C# solution and .csproj files automatically 🎮 Project Type This project is structured as a game, using C# as the scripting language and cfEngine as the backbone for: 💡 Integration Highlights ✅ C#-based scripting with Godot 4.4.1 ⚙️ Built-in cfEngine integration 🧱 Flexible foundation for prototyping and production 🧪 Running the Game Press F5 or click the Play icon in the Godot Editor. For code editing, use: Visual Studio 2022+ JetBrains Rider Any .NET-compatible IDE 📄 Exporting To export builds: Install export templates from Editor > Manage Export Templates Set up export presets via Project > Export Target any platform: Windows / macOS / Linux Android / iOS Web (HTML5) 📚 Documentation ➡️ Getting Started Guide ➡️ cfGodotEngine Built with ❤️ using Godot 4.4.1 (Mono) and .NET 8
